### How to Handle Your Hurt
Author: Betsy St. Amant Haddox
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/your-daily-bible-verse-march-21.html
Passage: Exodus 14:14
Points:
- When hurt or offended, people often rush to friends seeking validation instead of turning to God first.
- Speaking too quickly in the heat of pain frequently leads to gossip, slander, and additional conflict.
- In Exodus 14, Moses told the panicked and complaining Israelites to be silent and watch God act.
- Bringing emotional wounds to the Lord in prayer provides a safe refuge, true comfort, and lasting peace.
- Waiting quietly on God acknowledges that the battle belongs to Him and He already holds the victory.

### When You Feel Forgotten
Author: Cindi McMenamin
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/when-you-feel-forgotten-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Exodus 14:14
Points:
- Bleak circumstances and delays can make believers panic and feel overlooked or abandoned by God.
- Backed against the Red Sea, the Israelites were instructed not to fear but to stand still and trust God to fight for them.
- God miraculously parted the waters and delivered His people while overwhelming the pursuing Egyptian army.
- Despite witnessing God's supernatural power, people often quickly forget His past faithfulness and begin to grumble.
- Scripture promises that God never forgets His children; the only thing He chooses to forget is confessed sin.
